title: 69 tries: the first time a 1% chance passes 50%

evidence.proof: Complement rule with independent Bernoulli trials: P(no success) = 0.99^100. Therefore P(at least one) = 1 - 0.99^100.

caption:
A 1% chance per try. When does the chance of at least one success first pass 50%?

With the same 1% chance on every independent try:
68 tries: 1 - 0.99^68 ≈ 49.51%.
69 tries: 1 - 0.99^69 ≈ 50.016%, the first time above 50%.
100 tries: 1 - 0.99^100 ≈ 63.4%.

Why? The chance of no successes is 0.99^n. Subtract that from1. The colored area shows a probability, not the number of successful tries or a simulated result.

Independence and an identical 1% chance matter. These are model probabilities, not a guarantee. Original code-drawn animation and synthesized sound cues.
